text:
Jamie S (Sales): hey team, acme is blocked on POC onboarding — they enabled SSO and now user provisioning via SCIM fails with a 403. timeline: they completed SAML with the IdP but SCIM writes are rejected. can we triage? :eyes:
Devon (Platform SE): thanks — can you paste the exact SCIM response and the token scope used?
Jamie S (Sales): copied from their console:
```
HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "status":403,
  "error":"forbidden",
  "message":"token missing required scope: scim.write"
}
```
Jamie S (Sales): they say they used the service account token we provided in the hosted POC workspace, nothing else changed.
Ayesha (Customer Admin): fwiw we did rotate the token after the SSO switch because we thought auth would change. we may have used the wrong client creds.
Devon (Platform SE): ok two possibilities: 1) token is for SSO-only session (no scim scope) 2) during the SAML IdP flow we created a shadow user that isn't allowed to call SCIM. can you confirm the token string prefix (just first 6 chars) and whether it's a service token vs ephemeral user token?
Ayesha (Customer Admin): token starts with "rwd_9f3a2b" — looks like the service token format.
Devon (Platform SE): looks like a service token, good. can you run `curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/scim/Users` and paste response (sanitized)?
Ayesha (Customer Admin): response shows the same 403 and this body: 
```json
{
  "error": "insufficient_scope",
  "required": ["scim.read","scim.write"],
  "provided": ["scim.read"]
}
```
Marta (Security): this suggests the client was issued read-only scopes. are you using the token from the 'Hosted POC' -> Tokens page or the one generated by the Okta provisioning app?
Ayesha (Customer Admin): we grabbed the token from the Okta provisioning integration in their tenant (we thought that would auto-provision).
okta_bot: Provisioning sync failed at 2024-08-14T15:02:13Z — HTTP 403 returned during SCIM PATCH /Users. See provisioning logs in Okta admin.
okta_bot: Last sync attempt 3/3 failures.
Jamie S (Sales): 🤦 Okta provisioning created an OIDC client that only requested scim.read in the initial setup. Devon, can we add scim.write without redoing the whole SAML config?
Devon (Platform SE): yes — if the Okta app is using a custom OAuth client we can update the scope list on the client to include scim.write and then rotate the token. if Okta is using our prebuilt integration, there is a toggle in the admin UI. step-by-step: 1) update Okta app scopes to include `scim.write` and `groups.write` 2) re-trigger provisioning (push) 3) validate with `GET /scim/ServiceProviderConfig` and a test user creation.
Devon (Platform SE): in the meantime, quick workaround: create a new service token in Hosted POC -> Tokens with full scim scopes and share to customer (rotate after). that gets them unblocked for the demo.
Marta (Security): if you do that, we need an audit entry and short TTL on the temp token. request expiration 24h and require rotation after demo. also log the token issuance in the security tracker.
Ryan (SRE): noted — I can add an automatic tag for POC-temp tokens so they show up in our audits.
Ayesha (Customer Admin): ok we'll try creating a new service token first. can someone confirm the minimal scopes needed for group sync?
Devon (Platform SE): groups: `groups.read` + `groups.write`. users: `scim.read` + `scim.write`. for full provisioning include both sets.
Ayesha (Customer Admin): created new token, initial test user creation worked :tada:. pushed to Okta provisioning -> still failing on group pushes with 403.
Devon (Platform SE): can you paste the Okta provisioning logs for the group push? often Okta uses a different endpoint for group sync that maps to `PATCH /Groups/{id}` and requires `groups.write`.
Ayesha (Customer Admin): Okta log snippet:
```
[2024-08-14T15:10:22Z] POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/scim/Groups/bulk/push 403 Forbidden
{
  "error":"insufficient_scope",
  "required":["groups.write"],
  "provided":["scim.write","scim.read"]
}
```
Devon (Platform SE): Ah — your new token has scim scopes but not `groups.write`. our token UI labels are confusing. I'll update the UI copy. for now, create a token including `groups.write`.
Jamie S (Sales): Ayesha — want me to create the temporary token with groups.write and send via secure share?
Ayesha (Customer Admin): yes please, that would be helpful.
Marta (Security): reminder — temp token to be marked POC and TTL 12h. no long-lived secrets.
Ryan (SRE): I'll add an alert to our token registry for tokens created in the `sales/poc` org.
Jamie S (Sales): done, shared secure link to Ayesha. she confirmed group push now succeeds.
Ayesha (Customer Admin): confirmed all provisioning tests pass, users + groups synced, demo green. thank you! :green_heart:
Devon (Platform SE): follow-up: we'll add an entry to the onboarding checklist to verify Okta app scopes and token origin (Hosted UI vs Okta auto-client).
Marta (Security): also adding a line to the POC security runbook: require explicit scim scopes in Okta provisioning and short TTL for temp tokens.
Jamie S (Sales): closing the blocker. thanks team. :shipit:
Devon (Platform SE): leaving note — potential future: support mapping from Okta app to scopes automatically at install time. filing an infra task.
okta_bot: Integration status: healthy (post-fix)
Jamie S (Sales): marking resolved on the deal thread and notifying AE.
